title: General Physics I (Mechanics)
description: The first physics course, taught as PHY 102: Introductory Mechanics and Properties of Matter before the CCMAS codes: useful mathematics, quantities, units and dimensions, vectors, kinematics, Newton's laws, gravitation, work and energy, rotating rigid bodies, simple harmonic motion, elasticity and some properties of liquids. Built from the PHY 102 slides of Prof. O. E. Awe and Dr T. Ogunseye and the elasticity, work and rotation notes, with the CA tests and exam pages labelled with the former code.

topics.title: Units, Dimensions and Useful Mathematics
topics.summary: Physical quantities are fundamental or derived, each with SI units and a dimension in terms of M, L and T. Dimensional analysis checks equations and derives relations, and logarithmic graphs, derivatives and integrals are the mathematical tools of mechanics.
subtopics: Checking equations and deriving relations by dimensions

topics.title: Vectors
topics.summary: Scalars have magnitude only, while vectors have magnitude and direction. Vectors are added by the triangle rule and the cosine and sine rules, or by components in i, j, k notation, and multiplied as dot and cross products.
subtopics: Geometric addition: cosine and sine rules
Components and i, j, k notation
Dot product, cross product and area

topics.title: Kinematics and Projectiles
topics.summary: Kinematics describes motion without asking about its causes. It covers velocity and acceleration as rates of change, the constant-acceleration equations, free fall, and projectiles whose horizontal and vertical motions are treated separately.
subtopics: Oblique projectiles: height, time of flight and range

topics.title: Newton's Laws, Friction and Circular Motion
topics.summary: Newton's laws connect force to motion: inertia, F = ma and action–reaction. Friction on rough planes, connected bodies, and the centripetal force of circular motion are the main applications in PHY 101.
subtopics: Connected bodies and the Atwood machine
Uniform circular motion and centripetal acceleration

topics.title: Gravitation
topics.summary: Every two masses attract with a force proportional to their masses and inversely proportional to the square of their distance. This law gives g at a planet's surface, the orbits of satellites, escape speeds and the weight of bodies on other planets.
subtopics: Variation of weight with mass and radius
Satellites, orbital speed and parking orbits

topics.title: Work, Energy and Rotating Rigid Bodies
topics.summary: Work is force times displacement along it, and energy is the capacity to do work, conserved when only conservative forces act. A rotating rigid body has a moment of inertia, angular momentum and rotational kinetic energy, the rotational counterparts of mass, momentum and kinetic energy.
subtopics: Work as a dot product; power
Kinetic and potential energy; the work–energy theorem
Moment of inertia and the parallel axes theorem
Torque, angular momentum and rotational kinetic energy

topics.title: Simple Harmonic Motion, Elasticity and Liquids
topics.summary: Simple harmonic motion is oscillation under a restoring force proportional to displacement, as in springs and pendulums. Elastic solids obey Hooke's law, described by Young's, bulk and shear moduli, and liquids show pressure, buoyancy, surface tension and viscosity.
subtopics: Restoring force and the SHM equation
Bulk modulus and modulus of rigidity
Properties of liquids: pressure, upthrust, surface tension, viscosity
